name: Jaimini

tradition.text: pupil of Vyāsa, to whom Vyāsa entrusted the Sāmaveda (Purāṇic account)

scholarly.text: the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra c. 3rd c. BCE – 1st c. CE

notes: The Purāṇic Jaimini (Sāmaveda transmitter, narrator of the Jaimini Aśvamedha) and the sūtrakāra are identified by tradition; the identity is not established historically. The astrological Jaimini Sūtras (src:jaimini-upadesa-sutra) are a separate attribution.
summary: Author of the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra. In the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra he is cited by name for positions (e.g. that actions too are subsidiaries, MS 3.1.4); the Brahma Sūtra reports his views on the fruit of action, on knowledge as subsidiary to rites and on the released self (BS 3.2.40, 3.4.2, 3.4.18, 4.3.12, 4.4.5).

name: Bādarāyaṇa
notes: Identified with Vyāsa in Vedānta tradition; Mīmāṃsā contribution only here.
summary: Cited in the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra as an authority: the injunction is valid 'in Bādarāyaṇa's view' because it depends on nothing else (MS 1.1.5); women are eligible for rites because the class is meant (MS 6.1.8); also MS 5.2.19, 10.8.44, 11.1.63. Author of the Brahma Sūtra.

name: Bādari
summary: Early Mīmāṃsā teacher cited in the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra: holds that only substances, qualities and purificatory acts are subsidiaries (MS 3.1.3) and that the injunctions are for all four varṇas (MS 6.1.27, a view rejected); also cited at MS 8.3.6 and in the Brahma Sūtra.

name: Aitiśāyana
summary: Early teacher cited in the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra, e.g. for the prima facie view that only men are eligible for rites because of the masculine gender in 'svargakāmo yajeta' (MS 6.1.6) and at MS 3.2.43.

name: Ātreya (Mīmāṃsā teacher)
notes: Disambiguated from other Ātreyas (e.g. of Āyurveda).
summary: Early teacher cited in the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra: the fruit stated for a rite is real, not mere praise (MS 4.3.18); only the three higher varṇas are eligible because the setting-up of the fires names only them (MS 6.1.26).

name: Kārṣṇājini
summary: Early teacher cited in the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra (MS 4.3.17, 6.7.35), e.g. holding that fruit-statements within a sacrifice are praise like those for subsidiaries.

name: Āśmarathya
summary: Early teacher cited in the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra on a ritual detail of the new-moon rite (MS 6.5.16); also cited in the Brahma Sūtra.

name: Ālekhana
summary: Early teacher cited in the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra (MS 6.5.17).

name: Lābukāyana
summary: Early teacher cited in the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra (MS 6.7.37; spelled Lāvukāyana in one edition).

name: Kāmukāyana
summary: Early teacher cited in the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra (MS 11.1.56, 11.1.61).

name: Upavarṣa
notes: Whether Upavarṣa is the same as the Vṛttikāra quoted by Śabara, or as Bodhāyana (the Vṛttikāra of Rāmānuja's tradition), is disputed.
summary: Called 'the revered (bhagavān) Upavarṣa' by Śabara, who cites his view that the word 'gauḥ' is simply the letters g, au and ḥ; Śaṅkara (BSBh 3.3.53) reports that Upavarṣa in the first treatise deferred the proof of the self to the Śārīraka.

name: the Vṛttikāra (cited by Śabara)
notes: Identity disputed (Upavarṣa? Bodhāyana? Bhavadāsa?). Scholarly literature calls this passage the Vṛttikāragrantha.
summary: An earlier commentator whose exposition Śabara reproduces on MS 1.1.3–5 ('the Vṛttikāra explained this passage otherwise'): definitions of perception, inference, verbal testimony, comparison, postulation and absence as means of knowledge, a refutation of the views that cognitions have no object and that all is empty, and a proof of the self.

name: Bhavadāsa
summary: Commentator on the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra before Kumārila, who mentions him (ŚV pratijñā 63); the Nyāyaratnākara reports that he split MS 1.1.4 into two sūtras. His work is lost.

name: Śabarasvāmin

realization_account.text: A late popular verse makes Śabarasvāmin, a brāhmaṇa, the father by wives of the four varṇas of Varāhamihira, King Vikramāditya, Bhartṛhari and others; another story says he lived disguised as a śabara (forest-dweller). These are legends, not Mīmāṃsā doctrine.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Legend details are from memory (low confidence).
summary: Author of the Śābarabhāṣya, the earliest surviving commentary on the whole Mīmāṃsā Sūtra and the base text of both later schools.

name: Bhartṛmitra
summary: Pre-Kumārila Mīmāṃsaka whom the Nyāyaratnākara names among those who had made Mīmāṃsā 'Lokāyata' (ŚV pratijñā 10) — by the commentators' account, by denying that obligatory and prohibited acts bear fruit. His work is lost.

name: Kumārila Bhaṭṭa

tradition.text: older contemporary of Śaṅkara, whom he met at Prayāga at the end of his life (Śaṅkaradigvijaya)

realization_account.text: Hagiographies of Śaṅkara (e.g. the Śaṅkaradigvijaya ascribed to Mādhava-Vidyāraṇya) present Kumārila as an incarnation of Skanda sent to restore the Vedic path; they tell that he studied among Buddhists, survived a fall from a height by the truth of the Veda, and later entered a husk-fire at Prayāga as expiation, where Śaṅkara met him and was sent on to Maṇḍana Miśra.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: Hagiographic details are from memory and are not in Kumārila's works (low confidence). The teacher–pupil link with Prabhākara is a Bhāṭṭa legend; its historicity is doubted.
summary: Founder of the Bhāṭṭa school: author of the Ślokavārttika, Tantravārttika and Ṭupṭīkā on Śabara, and a lost Bṛhaṭṭīkā. He defended the authorless Veda and intrinsic validity against Buddhists, rejected omniscience in matters of dharma, a creator and a total dissolution, and set out a path to release through avoidance of desire-prompted and prohibited acts.

name: Prabhākara Miśra

tradition.text: a pupil of Kumārila who earned the title 'Guru' when he construed a passage his teacher could not (Bhāṭṭa story)

scholarly.text: c. 7th c. CE; relation to Kumārila uncertain

notes: 'teachers' records the tradition's claim only; the story of the title is from memory (low). Śālikanātha as a direct pupil is the tradition's view.
summary: Founder of the Prābhākara school ('Guru'): author of the Bṛhatī and the lost Laghvī on Śabara. Taught five means of knowledge, self-luminous cognition, error as non-apprehension and the kārya-centred meaning of Vedic sentences.

name: Maṇḍana Miśra

realization_account.text: In Śaṅkara's hagiographies Maṇḍana, a ritualist householder, debates Śaṅkara with his wife Ubhaya-Bhāratī as judge, is defeated, takes sannyāsa and becomes Sureśvara.
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

notes: The identification with Sureśvara is traditional and disputed by modern scholarship.
summary: Mīmāṃsaka of the Bhāṭṭa line (by tradition Kumārila's pupil): author of the Vidhiviveka (injunction means 'being a means to the desired'), Bhāvanāviveka, Vibhramaviveka, Mīmāṃsānukramaṇī, the Sphoṭasiddhi (defending sphoṭa) and the Advaita Brahmasiddhi.

name: Ubhaya-Bhāratī
summary: Wife of Maṇḍana Miśra in Śaṅkara's hagiographies, learned in the śāstras, who acts as judge of the debate between Maṇḍana and Śaṅkara and is presented as an incarnation of Sarasvatī.

name: Umbeka
notes: Identification with Bhavabhūti is traditional and disputed; being Kumārila's direct pupil is also traditional.
summary: Early commentator on the Ślokavārttika (Tātparyaṭīkā) and on Maṇḍana's Bhāvanāviveka; tradition identifies him with the dramatist Bhavabhūti.

name: Śālikanātha Miśra
notes: Direct discipleship of Prabhākara is traditional.
summary: Principal systematizer of the Prābhākara school: author of the Prakaraṇapañcikā and of the Ṛjuvimalā and Dīpaśikhā on Prabhākara's works.

name: Vācaspati Miśra
summary: Polymath commentator; for Mīmāṃsā he wrote the Nyāyakaṇikā on Maṇḍana's Vidhiviveka and the Tattvabindu on sentence meaning (defending abhihitānvaya).

name: Sucarita Miśra
summary: Author of the Kāśikā commentary on the Ślokavārttika.

name: Jayamiśra
summary: Author of the Śarkarikā commentary on the Ślokavārttika.

name: Pārthasārathi Miśra
summary: Leading Bhāṭṭa author: the Śāstradīpikā (independent commentary on the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra), Nyāyaratnākara (on the Ślokavārttika), Nyāyaratnamālā and Tantraratna. He defined a means of knowledge as a cognition apprehending what was not apprehended, free from defects of cause and from contradicting cognition, and held release to be the end of the threefold bond, without bliss.

name: Someśvara Bhaṭṭa
summary: Author of the Nyāyasudhā ('Rāṇaka') on the Tantravārttika.

name: Paritoṣa Miśra
summary: Author of the Ajitā commentary on the Tantravārttika.

name: Bhavadeva Bhaṭṭa
summary: Author of the Tautātitamatatilaka, an exposition of Kumārila's doctrine.

name: Bhavanātha
summary: Prābhākara author of the Nayaviveka.

name: Varadarāja (commentator on the Nayaviveka)
summary: Author of the Nayavivekadīpikā on Bhavanātha's Nayaviveka.

name: Nandīśvara
summary: Prābhākara author of the Prābhākaravijaya.

name: Rāmānujācārya (Prābhākara author)
summary: Late Prābhākara author of the Tantrarahasya; distinct from the Vedāntin Rāmānuja.

name: Murāri Miśra
notes: Modern literature numbers several Murāris inconsistently (II/III); low confidence on dating and on the second work.
summary: Mīmāṃsaka whose distinct account of how validity is known (through the after-cognition, anuvyavasāya) made him proverbially the founder of a 'third path'; fragments of his Tripādīnītinayana and (attributed) Aṅgatvanirukti survive.

name: Mādhava (Vidyāraṇya)
notes: The identification of Mādhava with the monk Vidyāraṇya is traditional and disputed; registry id used.
summary: For Mīmāṃsā: Mādhava, minister and family preceptor of King Bukka of Vijayanagara, composed the Jaiminīya-nyāya-mālā with its prose Vistara, a verse digest of all the adhikaraṇas.

name: Vedānta Deśika
summary: For Mīmāṃsā: author of the Seśvaramīmāṃsā, a theistic commentary on the Mīmāṃsā Sūtra, and the Mīmāṃsāpādukā.

name: Appayya Dīkṣita
summary: For Mīmāṃsā: author of the Vidhirasāyana (on the kinds of injunction) and the Upakramaparākrama (on the priority of the opening statement), among other works.

name: Śaṅkara Bhaṭṭa
summary: Son of Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭa; author of the Mīmāṃsābālaprakāśa and a critique of Appayya's Vidhirasāyana.

name: Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭa (Mānameyodaya)
notes: Identification with the author of the Nārāyaṇīyam is traditional; low confidence.
summary: Kerala scholar credited with the first (means-of-knowledge) part of the Mānameyodaya; traditionally identified with Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭatiri of Melpattūr.

name: Khaṇḍadeva Miśra
summary: Seventeenth-century Vārāṇasī Bhāṭṭa master: author of the Bhāṭṭadīpikā, Mīmāṃsākaustubha and Bhāṭṭarahasya, known for sharp Bhāṭṭa semantics in a Navya-Nyāya idiom.

name: Śambhu Bhaṭṭa
summary: Pupil of Khaṇḍadeva; author of the Prabhāvalī on the Bhāṭṭadīpikā.

name: Āpadeva
summary: Son of Anantadeva; author of the Mīmāṃsānyāyaprakāśa ('Āpadevī'), a standard introduction to Bhāṭṭa Mīmāṃsā that dedicates dharma to Govinda.

name: Laugākṣi Bhāskara
summary: Author of the Arthasaṅgraha, a beginner's primer of Bhāṭṭa Mīmāṃsā closely following Āpadeva, and of the Tarkakaumudī (Nyāya-Vaiśeṣika).

name: Kṛṣṇa Yajvan
summary: Author of the Mīmāṃsāparibhāṣā, an elementary manual.

name: Gāgā Bhaṭṭa
notes: His role in Śivājī's coronation (1674) is well known; not a Mīmāṃsā teaching.
summary: Vārāṇasī scholar (Viśveśvara Bhaṭṭa) of the Bhaṭṭa family; author of the Bhāṭṭacintāmaṇi.

name: Nārāyaṇa Tīrtha
notes: Whether he is the same as the devotional composer Nārāyaṇa Tīrtha is uncertain.
summary: Author of the Bhāṭṭabhāṣāprakāśa.

name: Devasvāmin
summary: Author of a bhāṣya on the Saṅkarṣa-kāṇḍa.

name: Somanātha Dīkṣita
summary: Author of the Mayūkhamālikā on the Śāstradīpikā.

name: Rāmakṛṣṇa Bhaṭṭa
summary: Author of the Yuktisnehaprapūraṇī on the tarkapāda of the Śāstradīpikā.

name: Vāsudeva Dīkṣita
summary: Author of the Adhvaramīmāṃsākutūhalavṛtti on the whole Mīmāṃsā Sūtra.
